directAnswer: You can back up your Android phone using the built-in Google Backup feature or by manually transferring files to a computer.
summary: Backing up your Android phone ensures that your data is safe and can be restored if needed.

sections.heading: Using Google Backup
sections.body: Google Backup allows you to automatically back up your app data, call history, contacts, and settings. Ensure you are connected to Wi-Fi for larger backups.

sections.heading: Manual Backup to Computer
sections.body: You can also manually back up your photos, videos, and documents by connecting your phone to a computer and transferring the files.

steps.title: Enable Google Backup
steps.detail: Go to Settings > System > Backup. Toggle on 'Back up to Google Drive'.

steps.title: Check Backup Settings
steps.detail: In the Backup menu, ensure that the data types you want to back up are selected.

steps.title: Transfer Files Manually
steps.detail: Connect your phone to a computer via USB, select 'File Transfer' mode, and copy the desired files to your computer.

faqs.question: How do I know if my backup was successful?
faqs.answer: You can check the last backup time in Settings > System > Backup under 'Back up to Google Drive'.

faqs.question: Can I back up my apps?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you enable Google Backup, your app data will be included, but not all apps support this feature.

faqs.question: Is there a limit to how much I can back up?
faqs.answer: Google Drive offers 15 GB of free storage; additional storage requires a subscription.

caveats: Some data, like certain app settings or files stored on the SD card, may not be included in the backup.
